text:
Alexander Kerfoot is in Nashville now, his fifth NHL stop, playing more than 16 minutes a night on a team that has won four straight. He's a penalty killer who rarely shoots: 13 shots in 17 games, two goals and six points.

The Predators have a slightly better chance share with him on the ice than without him (50% of the five-on-five expected goals, the quality of chances), and they've scored 4.3 fewer goals than those chances deserve when he's out there, which has cost him assists. He has two points in his last ten games.

Evolving-Hockey had his value last season coming mostly on defense, with opponents getting fewer chances with him out there (88th percentile), though from a small sample. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking said 60% of his shots came off the rush. He was a fifth-round pick in 2012 who went to Harvard and has stuck for more than 650 games. Our projection sees about 36 points. His value won't be in that number.
